title: Axial Airflow and Hub Position Configurator
description: Eight axial fan orders in which the learner commits a hub position and a hub bore before the fan is drawn and animated, followed by a free model that switches the airflow code between PM and MP and reverses the rotation.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
educational.topic: Axial airflow codes, hub position and hub bore
learningObjectives: The learner will apply FanPedia's axial airflow rules to state the hub position and hub bore for an axial fan order, given its airflow code or air path, with at least 7 of 8 orders correct.
prerequisites: rotation viewed from the discharge side

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); every verdict, new order and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; chosen answers are marked with aria-pressed, a ✓ and a heavier outline; keys I/D (hub side), S/R (bore) and Enter (check, next); every control is reachable with Tab; controls stay inside the canvas at 320 px.

rules: PM gives hub on intake side and reverse bore hub
MP gives hub on discharge side and standard bore hub
Impeller hand (left or right) and pitch type (fixed or adjustable) do not change hub position or bore
Reversible impeller: standard flow = MP, reverse flow = PM
Correct rotation: air enters at the leading edges and leaves at the discharge; reversed rotation: no airflow in the intended direction
Rotation is always labeled as viewed from the discharge side
An order is correct only when both answers match; one attempt per order; mastery 7 of 8 on the first attempt
assumptions: Direct-drive axial fan drawn with the motor at the left of the tube and the impeller at the right
The hub boss is drawn on the impeller face away from the motor, which faces the intake for PM and the discharge for MP
limitations: The rotation arrow means 'correct for the impeller' or 'reversed'; the impeller hand, and so the actual CW or CCW direction, is not modeled
Schematic drawing, not a specific Twin City Fan model

sources: FanPedia PDF pp. 36-40: airflow codes PM and MP, 'aka' hub names, leading edge, rotation viewing side, wrong-rotation note
FanPedia PDF p. 41: reversible impeller standard and reverse flow
FanPedia PDF pp. 42-43: standard bore hub with MP and reverse bore hub with PM, left and right hand, adjustable and fixed cast impellers

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Apply a rule set to new orders with a committed, checked answer; animate the air path only after the answer, then explore the model freely
keyQuestions: Which part does the air meet first in PM, and in MP?
Why does a reversible impeller have two hub positions?
What happens to the airflow when an axial impeller turns the wrong way?
commonMisconceptions: 'Hub on intake' means the motor is on the intake side
PM and MP are rotation codes rather than airflow codes
A reversible impeller has a fixed hub position
Running an axial impeller backward simply gives less airflow in the same direction
assessmentOpportunities: Running count shown as 'Orders correct: n of 8'; mastery is 7 of 8 orders on the first attempt.
